summary: Dedicated capacity uneven shard affinity causing GPU starvation and autoscaler oscillation during off-peak window
description:
Issue summary: NovusHealth observed an intermittent but sustained p50/p95 throughput degradation in their dedicated pool during a nightly off-peak window (approx 02:00-04:30 UTC). Requests queue and remain pending for several seconds despite spare GPU capacity reported across the cluster. Impact: customer-facing latency regressions and elevated queue lengths for a production model pinned to redwood-open-7b-v2. Environment: Dedicated reserved pool (pool-id: p-7461), region us-west-2, model pinned to redwood-open-7b-v2, customer uses small streaming requests (avg tokens/output small).

Observed behavior: autoscaler repeatedly scales down and back up during the window (oscillation) with short lived GPU attach/detach events. Several GPUs appear underutilized while others are saturated (high NVLink/PCIe stalls). Allocator logs show placement-group affinity enforcement that groups long-lived connections onto the same GPU shards. Concurrently, we observe a high proportion of small, long-lived streams from the customer (50-200ms per stream) that serialize into tiny batches and prevent effective packing. Expected behavior: autoscaler should maintain steady capacity with minimal oscillation and scheduler should evenly balance affinity/shards to avoid localized starvation.

Why this is unique: the pattern is not a classic noisy-tenant burst – it's a fragmentation effect caused by affinity placement plus many small, long-lived streams which prevents the batcher and KV-cache from coalescing requests. This leads to allocation fragmentation and localized NVLink/PCIe contention even with nominal free GPU slots.

Relevant timestamps: first alert 2026-03-12T02:07:21Z, repeat window 02:00–04:30 UTC nightly, mitigations applied 2026-03-13 03:10Z.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a dedicated pool with placement-group affinity enabled (pool-id p-7461)
2) Launch many low-throughput, long-lived streaming connections (keepalive + small message size, avg 50ms per chunk) pinned to redwood-open-7b-v2
3) Observe autoscaler decisions around 02:00–04:30 UTC when background maintenance and predictive shrink triggers run
4) Monitor allocator logs for placement decisions and NVLink/PCIe stalls; watch the batcher for inability to form multi-request batches
impact: Customer NovusHealth experienced sustained throughput reduction (p95 latency up 3x) for a core inference route during nightly window; degraded user experience for automated reports generated in that window. Billing unaffected but SLA risk (P1).

2026-03-12T02:07:22Z autoscaler: scale_down candidate_reduction=2 pool=p-7461 reason=idle_estimate threshold_crossed
investigation_notes: Initial triage: SRE validated elevated queued request counts correlated with particular shards (shard 2/3/7).

Telemetry: high small-stream ratio from customer (~78% of active connections were streaming <200ms chunks) prevents batching algorithms from grouping requests; KV cache hit rate fell on affected shards.

Allocator hypothesis: placement-group affinity is forcing long-lived connections onto the same subset of GPUs. When combined with many tiny streams, this creates per-shard serialization and NVLink contention despite free slots elsewhere.
Reproduction on staging: reproduced by spinning many low-throughput streaming clients with affinity enabled; switching affinity off produced even distribution and eliminated queuing.

Correlation found between predictive autoscaler shrink window (02:00 UTC) and the oscillation: scale_down decisions do not account for small-stream serialization metric leading to over-shrink, then rapid scale-up.
Risk: applying affinity changes may affect customers relying on shard-local KV cache warmness; need staged rollout and communication to NovusHealth.
comments: Priya Khatri (Support) 2026-03-12T05:10Z: Notified SRE and customer; collecting traces and sample request ids.
Marcus Liu (SRE) 2026-03-12T06:02Z: Confirmed per-shard queueing. Attaching allocator and nvlink counters. Opening INT follow-up if we need config changes.

Ethan Park (Oncall Infra) 2026-03-13T03:12Z: Applied temp_scheduler_override to ignore affinity for p-7461 for 10 mins — immediate reduction in queued requests observed (p50_wait_ms down from 3100ms to 340ms).
NovusHealth (Customer) 2026-03-13T03:30Z: Thanks — saw improvement in dashboard. Concerned about long term stability and whether affinity is required for their deployment semantics.
Priya Khatri 2026-03-13T10:00Z: Planning next steps: controlled config change to scheduler to prefer soft-affinity and autoscaler tuning to include small-stream serialization metric.
resolution: Mitigation applied 2026-03-13: temporary scheduler override to ignore strict placement-group affinity for pool p-7461 reduced queuing and removed autoscaler oscillation. Next steps: 1) implement a soft-affinity mode that balances KV-warmth vs slot distribution (engineering ticket INT-9924), 2) augment autoscaler signals to include small-stream serialization ratio and NVLink stall counts, 3) coordinate with NovusHealth for a scheduled maintenance window to flip soft-affinity. Post-mortem scheduled and runbook updated.
follow_up_actions: Create engineering story INT-9924 to add soft-affinity mode and tests
Add autoscaler metric: small_stream_serialization_ratio and NVLink stall threshold to prevent premature shrink
Schedule maintenance with NovusHealth to validate soft-affinity on a staging slice
Draft customer-facing summary and preventive guidance for small-stream workloads
